content.text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. It is bonded to a second ring that bears OH, adjacent to the biaryl bond, and an NH–N= group on the carbon next to the OH. So this is 3'-hydrazinyl-2'-hydroxybiphenyl-3-carboxylic acid.

**Hydrazone and isatin part.** The NH–N= unit connects to C3 of an indolin-2-one. C2 is the C=O, and N1 carries an aryl group. That aryl group is 3-fluoro-4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl. The ring is attached at C1, F sits at C3, and CF3 sits at C4.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond is drawn with the NH on one side, but I am not assigning E/Z geometry.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)c(F)c3)c3ccccc23)c1O
- In the middle ring, the carbon bearing the aryl group is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH, which is adjacent to the carbon bearing the hydrazine.
- The ring closure `c1cccc(N...)c1O` places the aryl-bearing carbon first (c1), then three CH, then the carbon with the hydrazine, then the carbon with OH closing back to c1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)c(F)c3)c3ccccc23)c1O
